title: What every AI call carries
headline: The shopper chat is lean (about 5,000 characters of prompt and tools a call); the AI manager is the heavy part: about 161,700 characters a call (roughly 40,400 tokens, an estimate at 4 characters a token), 91% of it 124 tool definitions that do not depend on the question, on up to 11 calls a turn. A lean default drawn with the app's own functions is 48,600 characters on Home and 77,000 on an orders page; it is already step 3.18 of the code review, still Open, and the eval meant to guard it does not test whether the model finds a tool (9 manager cases, none uses load_tools), so that check comes first. Around the AI, screens, polls and five-minute jobs fetch the AI connection and walk every site before knowing there is work (237,563 connection reads against 19,104 AI calls): small today, rising with every store, clearest in the alt-text job. The one quick, safe win is in the browser: the chat's script is 496 KB, of which about 370 KB is the model's tool catalogue and admin map.

findings.title: Every AI manager call sends 124 tool definitions, whatever the question or screen
findings.evidence: chooseTools() fills the budget to the provider's cap: core tools, tools used before, the page's area, then every other area in a fixed order (tool-budget.ts:84-88). Run on a shop-only store it offers 234 store tools and sends 97 plus the manager's 26 and load_tools: 146,889 characters. The system prompt is 14,772. A round is about 161,700 characters, 91% tools. streamWithTools() gets the list on every round but a forced last one (owner-assistant.ts:793). I ran the skeptic's bundle again here and the numbers hold. My own draw of a lean choice (core, used, asked for, the page's area, no fill) gives 33,810 characters of tools on Home, 62,242 on an orders page, 65,146 on marketing, 81,807 on website, 86,581 on products and 88,609 on a settings page: the page's area can itself be large (settings 55 tools, website 41, marketing 32 to 40, products 28 to 30 with two tools of 11,000 characters each).
findings.cost: About 40,400 input tokens a call (estimate at 4 characters a token; JSON tokenises worse, so a floor), up to 11 calls a turn; about 121,000 tokens for a turn with two tool rounds, about 3 cents at the seeded gpt-5-mini price before any provider cache discount, more on a larger model. It also uses up a store's monthly AI allowance at the full price. This cost follows use, so it is small today; it is the AI cost that grows fastest once many owners use the manager (an illustration, not a forecast: 1,000 stores x 10 turns a day x 3 calls is about 1.2 billion input tokens a day).
findings.who_pays: The server per AI manager call: Kaizena Flow's provider bill for stores on its key, the store's monthly AI allowance (or its own key), and the owner waiting for the answer.

findings.evidence: aiFor() has no cache: each call runs 'select * from commerce.ai_providers', decrypts up to three API keys and, for a store on Kaizena Flow's key whose plan sets an AI limit, reads the limits and sums the month's ai_usage (a 60-second memo per server instance, limits.ts:122-144). My rg finds it on 89 lines in 64 files outside ai.ts and tests. Many want only a yes or no: the staff's open conversation calls it on every poll for the Translate button (support-inbox.ts:98; every 2 seconds without a realtime connection, every 15 with one or while hidden); opening a page in the builder calls it three times in a row through canMakePictures(), canEditPictures() and canChangePages() (pages/context.ts:165-168); the product editor once (products.ts:196); the AI manager's panel and the page studio once each for their abilities. Production: 237,563 provider reads and 8,514 cost sums against 19,104 recorded AI calls. Those counts are scheduled work, builds and the team's own testing, not shoppers.
findings.cost: Today small: each provider read is a sub-millisecond query on a tiny table plus a round trip; the dear part is the cost sum (37 to 57 ms, about 352 s in 78 days). What grows: the sum runs only for stores whose plan sets an AI limit, which today's template and demo stores mostly are not and paying stores will be; and every open support conversation, builder page and product editor adds reads in step with the owners at work.

findings.title: The knowledge, product and picture index jobs rescan per store to find nothing
findings.evidence: Knowledge: every five minutes, for each site with a chat agent, the job selects every published page and article with its whole published JSON to compare one timestamp (about 40 pages a call, 24,134 calls). A published page that yields no passages has no chunk row, so it is cut and 'replaced' again on every run: 91,200 delete calls removed 782 rows in all. Products: every run one statement computes an md5 over the title, terms and description of every active product translation of every store on the platform's AI (embeddings.ts:31-52; 10,201 calls, 14.5 ms with about 300 products). Products are embedded when saved in the editor, the translator, a bulk edit, an import and a store copy, but not when the AI manager or a content pack saves one (product-tools.ts:221 and content-packs.ts:417 call saveProduct() with no refresh after it), so the scan is also how those reach search by meaning. Pictures: every run, for each site with media, the job fetches the AI connection, deletes vectors of undescribed pictures and selects stale ones (media-library.ts:860-873, 798-812; 49,842 calls at 0.4 ms); once a day per picture it looks up where each is used (145 ms mean) and usually only moves the date on (13,414 updates on 468 rows).
findings.cost: Database time in 78 days from the statements the skeptic matched: page reads for knowledge 42 s, picture uses 266 s, the product md5 scan 148 s, the stale-picture select 19 s: roughly 480 s, about 6 s a day. Small today, with one or two sites in each loop. What grows: knowledge and pictures loop per store, one after another, every five minutes; the product scan reads every product's text on the platform every five minutes as one statement under the 15 s limit (at 14.5 ms for about 300 products, a million product translations would be tens of seconds: an estimate by simple proportion).
findings.who_pays: The database and the dispatcher's function, every five minutes; more with every store that opens.

For each listed site, one after another, the loop fetches the AI connection (aiFor(), line 238), reads the site's languages (altSite()) and runs the exact due check (dueForAltText(), lines 201-214), and goes on until it has found five sites with work (line 236). When everything is up to date it walks them all, every five minutes. The verified report called this list 'already narrowed'; it is narrow only before the first alt text is written. Second, a picture whose alt text fails is marked tried (lines 104-107, 129, 136) and is due again after a day, each time fetching the picture and, for a provider error or an answer that could not be used, sending it to the vision model again (lines 119-136). The retries: one vision call a day on the store's allowance (or Kaizena Flow's bill for its own site) for every picture that cannot be described, for as long as the picture exists; capped only by the job's 4 pictures a site and 5 sites a run.

findings.evidence: Owner question 8 of the code review says a new eval run 'has to show it still finds the right tool'. The eval has 9 AI manager cases (rg counts them). Seven test that text planted in a tool's answer is not obeyed: they pass when no gated tool is called. Two require a tool: run_report, which is a core tool, and refund_order. For every case the harness loads the areas of all the tools the case scripts, forbids or requires before the first step (managerTools(), agent-eval.ts:146-153: 'so the tools a case tests are offered'). load_tools is handled if the model calls it (lines 188-192) but no case needs it, and rg finds the word nowhere in src/lib/agent-eval.ts. toolsVersion() hashes each tool's name, description and parameters (lines 78-81), not which tools a round sends, so a recording stays 'valid' when the default set changes. So today nothing would fail if a lean default left the model unable to find a tool, and nothing measures how well it finds one among 124 either.
findings.cost: No running cost. It is why the default sits at the provider's cap: the one change that would cut the AI manager's input by a third to two thirds (AI-1) has no check to pass. Every round of every turn pays for that until the check exists.
findings.who_pays: Every AI manager call, through AI-1 staying open; the team, who would otherwise learn of a missed tool from owners.
fix_steps: src/lib/agent-eval.ts: add `lean?: boolean` to AgentEvalCase and `loadsTools?: boolean` to its `expect` (the case passes only if load_tools was called before the required tool). Add six to eight manager cases marked lean, each a plain owner request whose tool is outside the core 12, with a scripted answer for that tool and `requiredTools`: a discount code (create_discount), a newsletter (a broadcast tool), free shipping over an amount (set_flat_shipping or save_shipping_method), a change to a page's text (get_page then edit_page), inviting staff (invite_staff), the plan and its price (billing_overview), a product's stock (set_stock), and one in Norwegian ('Lag en rabattkode på 10 %'). Add two that must not load anything: 'How many orders last week?' (run_report or list_orders) and a greeting. Check each tool name exists (src/lib/agent-eval.test.ts does).

src/server/agent-eval.ts, managerTools() (lines 146-153): for a lean case, do not preload: start from what a real turn on Home would send (core tools, the manager's own, load_tools, and the router's area once AI-1 is in), and add areas only as the model's load_tools calls ask (the loop at lines 188-192 already records them in `wanted`).

Same file, scoreAgentCase's caller: count a lean case as failed when the model answers that it cannot do the task without having called load_tools. Report, beside passed and total, how many lean cases needed a load_tools round: that number is the router's score.

toolsVersion() (lines 78-81): include what decides a round's tools (CORE_TOOLS, the load_tools definition for a fixed held-back set, TOOL_CHOICE_VERSION), so a recording made with one default set is refused for another.

Run the eval once on today's code with the new cases and keep the result as the 'before' (with 124 tools sent the lean cases should pass without load_tools; record how many do). Then AI-1 has something to be compared with.

Platform, AI: show the lean cases' result as its own line ('Finds its tools: 8 of 8, 3 with a load'). CLAUDE.md's Conventions paragraph on the eval: add that a change to which tools a round sends needs a new run, as a prompt change does.

findings.saving: None by itself. It unlocks AI-1 (a round down by 36% to 70%), AI-6 (15,384 characters a round) and AI-8, and keeps them from being undone unnoticed.
findings.risk: A handful of scripted cases is a smoke test, not proof: a model can pass them and still miss a real request. Keep the round log of AI-10 (load_tools calls, 'no tool' answers) as the check in production. Each eval run costs real model calls, a few cents with today's 9 cases and a lean tool set.
